# uptimekuma_status_page (Resource)

A public status page, with the groups of monitors shown on it.

~> **Three settings cannot be managed here.** `published`, the search-engine-index flag and the page password are read-only for any API client: the handler that saves a status page has those assignments commented out upstream, so no event can change them. Set them in the web UI.

~> **Group order is the display order.** Uptime Kuma derives each group's weight from its position, and the same goes for monitors inside a group, so `group` and `monitor` are ordered blocks rather than sets.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "uptimekuma_monitor_http" "web" {
  name = "Web"
  url  = "https://example.com"
}

resource "uptimekuma_monitor_http" "api" {
  name = "API"
  url  = "https://api.example.com/health"
}

resource "uptimekuma_status_page" "public" {
  slug  = "public"
  title = "Example Status"

  description = "Live status of our services"
  theme       = "auto"
  show_tags   = true
  footer_text = "Questions? support@example.com"

  # Group order is the display order, and so is monitor order inside a group.
  group {
    name = "Customer facing"

    monitor {
      monitor_id = uptimekuma_monitor_http.web.id
      send_url   = true
    }
  }

  group {
    name = "Internal"

    monitor {
      monitor_id = uptimekuma_monitor_http.api.id
    }
  }
}

output "status_page_url" {
  value = "https://kuma.example.com/status/${uptimekuma_status_page.public.slug}"
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `slug` (String) URL slug, so the page is served at `/status/<slug>`. Lowercased by the server.
- `title` (String) Title shown at the top of the page.

### Optional

- `analytics_id` (String) Site or tag ID for the analytics provider.
- `analytics_script_url` (String) Script URL for self-hosted analytics.
- `analytics_type` (String) Analytics provider: `google`, `umami`, `plausible`, `matomo` or `rybbit`.
- `auto_refresh_interval` (Number) How often the page refreshes itself, in seconds. Default: 300.
- `custom_css` (String) CSS injected into the page.
- `description` (String) Description shown under the title.
- `domain_names` (List of String) Custom domains that serve this page.
- `footer_text` (String) Text shown at the bottom of the page.
- `group` (Block List) A section of the page. Order matters: it is the display order, and a group left out of the configuration is deleted. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--group))
- `icon` (String) Logo for the page. Either a URL, or a `data:image/png;base64,...` value that the server stores as a file. PNG is the only accepted upload format. Default: `/icon.svg`.
- `rss_title` (String) Title of the page's RSS feed.
- `show_certificate_expiry` (Boolean) Show how long each certificate has left. Default: false.
- `show_only_last_heartbeat` (Boolean) Show only the most recent heartbeat instead of the bar. Default: false.
- `show_powered_by` (Boolean) Show the "Powered by Uptime Kuma" footer. Default: true.
- `show_tags` (Boolean) Show each monitor's tags. Default: false.
- `theme` (String) Page theme: `auto`, `light` or `dark`. Default: `auto`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The page's slug, which is how the API addresses it.
- `page_id` (Number) Numeric ID of the page. Use this for `uptimekuma_maintenance.status_page_ids`.
- `published` (Boolean) Whether the page is published. Read-only: no API event can change it.

<a id="nestedblock--group"></a>
### Nested Schema for `group`

Required:

- `name` (String) Heading for the section.

Optional:

- `monitor` (Block List) A monitor shown in this group, in display order. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--group--monitor))

<a id="nestedblock--group--monitor"></a>
### Nested Schema for `group.monitor`

Required:

- `monitor_id` (Number) ID of the monitor to show.

Optional:

- `send_url` (Boolean) Make the monitor's name a link. Default: false.
- `url` (String) Link the page shows for this monitor. Leave it unset to use the monitor's own URL, which the server then reports here. It is only reported at all when `send_url` is true, so with `send_url = false` Terraform cannot detect drift in it.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Status pages are imported by slug, not by numeric ID.
terraform import uptimekuma_status_page.example public
```
